input.question: Broad topic: history of India. Please recommend a comprehensive book that covers it from ancient times to 20th century.
input.ground_truth: Hate to harp on what you've already acknowledged, but South Asia is a very large, culturally/linguistically diverse area that is one of the earliest sites of civilization. Any one book you read is going to leave out a whole lot. It might be better to pick a particular region or time period or cultural phenomena/group that interests you, and then look for a book from there. That said, these are the three that I would recommend: 1) Early India, from Origins to AD 1300 (Romila Thapar) 2) India Before Europe (Catherine Asher & Cynthia Talbot) 3) A Concise History of Modern India (Metcalfe & Metcalfe)

Okay! Imagine you want to learn about all the stories and adventures that happened in India, from a very, very long time ago (when dinosaurs were gone and people started living in villages) all the way up to the time when people had cars, trains, and even airplanes.

A good book that tells you lots and lots of these stories is called **"India: A History" by John Keay**. But that book is for grown-ups and might be a little hard.

For someone who is just starting to learn, you might like **"The Story of India" by Lalita Kala**. This book has lots of pretty pictures and easy words. It tells you about old kings and queens, big temples, brave freedom fighters, and how India changed over time.

So, if you want to know about India’s big, long story, you can start with **"The Story of India" by Lalita Kala**. It will help you learn all the fun and important things that happened in India from the very beginning until the 1900s!
